---
title: "Average Daily Users"
description: "Distinct users on a typical day over a reporting window."
---

How many distinct users signed in to CanadaLogin on a typical day over a
selected reporting window: the mean of the daily unique-user counts.

**It is a typical day, not reach.** An average of 2,000 daily users over four
weeks does not mean 2,000 people used CanadaLogin in those four weeks; the same
person on ten different days counts on all ten. For how many different people
used it, read a cumulative column (see [Cumulative Unique
Users](cumulative-unique-users.qmd)). There is no unique-user count for an
arbitrary window such as "the last 28 days".

## Calculation

Average `unique_users` over the days in the window that have a row. Return the
number of days present beside it, and quote the average only when that equals
the number of days in the window. A missing day is a gap in the data, not a day
with no users: dividing by the length of the window would count it as zero and
pull the average down.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
SELECT
    AVG(CAST(unique_users AS DOUBLE)) AS average_daily_users,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CAST(from_date AS DATE)) AS days_present,
    -- the window's length, inclusive; quote the average only if they match
    date_diff('day', DATE '2026-09-03', DATE '2026-09-30') + 1 AS days_in_window
FROM ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_auth_total_logins
-- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE CAST(from_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-03' AND DATE '2026-09-30';
```

## R

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_auth_total_logins")) |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= as.Date("2026-09-03"),
    as.Date(from_date) <= as.Date("2026-09-30")
  ) |>
  summarise(
    average_daily_users = mean(as.double(unique_users), na.rm = TRUE),
    days_present = n_distinct(as.Date(from_date)),
    # the window's length, inclusive; quote the average only if they match
    days_in_window = !!(as.integer(as.Date("2026-09-30") - as.Date("2026-09-03")) + 1L)
  )
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

**Say "on a typical day" wherever it appears.** Readers take "average users" for
how many people use the service, which is a much larger number.

**Comparing two windows.** For a change against the previous window, use windows
of the same length and check both are complete. Weekends run lower than
weekdays, so a window should cover whole weeks: 28 days is four of each weekday.

**The rate behind other metrics.** Summing the same daily counts instead of
averaging them gives user-days, the denominator of [Calls per Active
User](../call_centre/calls-per-active-user.qmd).

## Alternative names

- daily active users
- DAU
- average daily active users
- typical daily users
